thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Trade Sharply Higher After Last Week's Rout; Trade Tensions Show Signs Of Cooling

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Trade Sharply Higher After Last Week's Rout; Trade Tensions Show Signs Of Cooling
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Treasury Sec. Mnuchin 'cautiously hopeful' over a trade deal with China
U.S. stocks jumped on Monday, with major indexes partially rebounding after their worst weekly performance in more than two years.
Trade issues continued to be a primary driver of market action, and reports that U.S. and China officials are conducting behind-the-scenes talks to avert a global trade war helped to erase some of the uncertainty spurred by recent policy pronouncements. A handful of Federal Reserve speakers may capture attention as well, as a holiday-shortened week of trading kicks off.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 494 points, or 2.1%, to 23,959. The S&P 500 was up 50 points, or 1.9%, to 2,638. The Nasdaq Composite Index gained 144 points to 7,136, a rise of 2.1%.
Monday is set to be the biggest one-day pop for the Dow and the Nasdaq since Feb. 6, and the best day for the S&P since March 9. However, that comes after a protracted period of weakness for Wall Street. The Dow closed Friday at its lowest level of the year, while all three indexes suffered their worst weekly returns since January 2016, when fears of a global economic rout dogged sentiment.
At current levels, the Dow is 10% below its record close while the S&P is 8.5% below its all-time high and the Nasdaq is 6.6% below its record.
What's driving markets?
Global trade tensions are expected to remain front and center for investors in what will be a holiday-shortened week, with markets scheduled to close in observance of Good Friday.
But equity traders seem to be taking some cheer in reports that China and the U.S (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-china-said-to-be-talking-behind-the-scene-to-avoid-trade-war-2018-03-25). have been holding discussions, in a bid to help stave off a trade war.
Those talks, led by U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin and Liu He, China's vice premier for economic policy, are aimed at providing better access to Chinese markets for U.S. companies. Tensions ratcheted up last week after the Trump administration declared tariffs on certain Chinese goods and China fired back with its own trade-related clampdown.
Mnuchin told Fox News on Sunday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mnuchin-says-hes-cautiously-hopeful-that-china-tariffs-can-be-avoided-2018-03-26) that he was "cautiously hopeful" an agreement can be reached with China.
Meanwhile, the U.S. and South Korea have reached a deal (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-south-korea-hammer-out-amended-trade-deal-2018-03-25) that will give the Asian country a permanent exemption from trade tariffs.
Read:The Dow may be at the mercy of politicians until earnings season (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-dow-may-be-at-the-mercy-of-politicians-until-earnings-season-2018-03-24)
What are strategists saying?
"The trade war is increasingly looking like a phony war. Even if U.S. trade policy is more spin than substance, increasing uncertainty does have implications for markets. Friday's budget veto hokey-cokey dance was also unsettling for investors. Market volatility is therefore likely to continue," said Paul Donovan, global chief economist at UBS, in a note to clients.
Read: How investors can protect against a trade war--in one sentence (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/how-investors-can-protect-against-a-trade-war-in-one-sentence-2018-03-14)
What is on the economic docket?
The Chicago Fed national activity index for February came in at 0.88, up from 0.02 in January.
Read: Is the pressure off? Inflation likely to die down in February, but don't get used to it (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/is-the-pressure-off-inflation-likely-to-die-down-in-february-but-dont-get-used-to-it-2018-03-24)
On Monday, New York Federal Reserve President William Dudley is scheduled to speak on regulatory reform in Washington, D.C. at 12:30 p.m. Eastern. Fed Vice Chair Randal Quarles is due to speak on consumer protection and small business at a forum in Atlanta at 7:10 p.m. Eastern.
Read: John Williams may be named New York Fed president: report (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/john-williams-may-be-named-new-york-fed-president-report-2018-03-25)
What stocks are in focus?
USG Corp.(USG) rejected an unsolicited buyout bid (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/usg-rejects-gebr-knaufs-unsolicited-buyout-bid-2018-03-26) by Gerb. Knauf AG, saying it "substantially undervalues" the company and is not in the best interest of its shareholders. The stock gained 18%.
Earlier, Berkshire Hathway Inc.(BRKA) (BRKA) offered to sell its 30.8% stake in the building materials group (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/usg-shares-jump-19-on-news-berkshire-offered-stake-to-knauf-entities-for-42share-2018-03-26) to privately held Gebr. Knauf Verwaltungsgesellschaft KG.
Finish Line Inc.(FINL) shares surged 30% after JD Sports Fashion PLC(JD.LN) said it would buy the U.S. retail chain for $13.50 per share in cash, in a deal valued at $558 million. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-finish-line-inc-announces-entry-into-merger-agreement-with-jd-sports-fashion-plc-2018-03-26)
Facebook Inc.(FB) fell 1%. The company continues to do damage control after the Cambridge Analytica data-privacy scandal, and took out full-page ads in nine U.S. and U.K. newspapers (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-apologizes-for-breach-of-trust-in-newspaper-ads-2018-03-25). The backlash has triggered a #DeleteFacebook movement. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/elon-musk-appears-to-have-joined-deletefacebook-2018-03-23) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/elon-musk-appears-to-have-joined-deletefacebook-2018-03-23)Facebook shares tumbled 14% last week.
Tech was a strong gainer on Monday, with Microsoft Corp.(MSFT) up 5%, Netflix Inc.(NFLX) adding 3.3%, and Apple Inc.(AAPL) and Amazon.com Inc.(AMZN) both gaining more than 2%.
Intel Corp.(INTC) rose 2.5% after Raymond James upgraded the stock to market perform (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/intel-stock-gains-as-raymond-james-upgrades-to-market-perform-despite-apple-concerns-2018-03-26), citing an improved supply/demand balance in the semiconductor industry.
Paychex Inc. (PAYX) jumped 3.6% after it reported third-quarter revenue that topped expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/paychexs-stock-surges-after-revenue-beat-upbeat-outlook-2018-03-26).
Biohaven Pharmaceutical Holding Co. Ltd. (BHVN) plummeted 31% after it released data (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/biohaven-shares-drop-23-after-migraine-drug-trial-results-2018-03-26-991513) from two phase 3 clinical trials for its migraine drug.
DarioHealth Corp. (DRIO) jumped 27% after it received FDA clearance (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dariohealth-stock-soars-after-iphone-compatible-glucose-monitor-receives-fda-clearance-2018-03-26) for its blood glucose monitoring system to be used on Apple iPhones.
What are other markets doing?
European equities were rallying off a one-year low (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-rally-from-1-year-low-2018-03-26). Asian markets finished mixed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-continue-to-pull-back-amid-trade-war-fears-2018-03-25), as losses eased toward the close, and the Korean Kospi Composite Index ended 0.5% higher after news of the U.S. trade agreement. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-strengthen-after-fed-raises-rates-2018-03-21)
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-strengthen-after-fed-raises-rates-2018-03-21)The ICE U.S. Dollar Index eased slightly, while gold dipped 0.1% to $1,348.40 an ounce.
Oil futures pulled back 0.3% to $65.76 a barrel. China's yuan-denominated crude-oil futures surged 3.3% on their debut Monday.
